page_checks.summary: Semantic middles retain active syntax and implied causers but often require modality, negation, or manner; cleaning/cutting and sell allow exceptions; five double-object lexical classes introduced.
Five verb classes: Oi+to, to-only, Oi+for, for-only, Oi-only; class membership is lexically and sense conditioned.
Double-object/prepositional alternations differ in information packaging, short pronoun order and recipient vs locative goal; communicative recipients and goods/service beneficiaries.
Goods beneficiary may permit Oi, service beneficiary usually uses for; Oi-only verbs may encode source, and ask/play/bear license other PP markers; strong dialect caveats.
Type II single core object corresponds to Oi of ditransitive and complements for/with; some British forms differ; Oi may be omitted with definite or indefinite implicit recipients.
Omission of beneficiary removes its participant, while omitting recipient may leave one understood; fine and tip retain indirect-object-like core under omission; supply/present/blame alternation.
Present/entrust/supply have lexical differences in oblique omissibility; spray/load theme-object versus locative-object alternation yields a restricted holistic interpretation.
Spray/load object governs completion conditions; put/fill restrict theme/locative object alignment, drain/remove/deprive differ in source and of/from complements.
Engrave/copy/label lexical theme-versus-locative object restrictions; hunt/search quest role; instrument versus theme alignment under hit/stab and obligatory locative.
Hit and throw/break contrasts show not every instrument/locative alternation preserves truth conditions; build/produce/change object aligns resultant goal or source with into/from PP.
Theme/locative subject alternation (abound/swam, flicker/sound) can imply a holistic affected location with with-PP; meaning difference limited by setting and preposition.
Develop/evolve source-goal subject switches, wash/wipe trivalent versus bivalent object alignment, fill/cover and instrumental or temporal PP participant becoming bivalent subject.

Noncore instrument/causer/theme/location/time/price arguments align as bivalent subject with verb-specific restrictions; combined complement can incorporate a prior object's body-part/property oblique.
Kiss/praise separate complement alternates with genitive/of NP combined object; increase/decrease measurable property may be expressed by subject or in-PP with shifted subject.
